purpose: Independent finite-shot feasibility/identifiability stress test of frozen QEC noise readout, not a sale or a hardware claim
pair_inventory: Evaluate all pairs of distinct pure registered noise hypotheses; disclose pairs with total variation <=1e-9 as numerically indistinguishable; choose the hardest distinguishable pair per fixture by maximum Bhattacharyya coefficient, lexicographic index tiebreak
primary_bound: With equal priors and N independent identical outcomes: error_opt(N)>=0.5*(1-sqrt(1-BC^(2N))) with BC=sum_i sqrt(p_i*q_i). Necessary N>=ceil(log(4alpha(1-alpha))/(2log(BC))) when 0<BC<1. This is NECESSARY, not sufficient; BC=1 is indistinguishable and BC=0 requires at least one shot.
conventional: Independently construct syndrome-space pair-specific one-shot Helstrom discrimination e=(1-0.5||rho-sigma||_1)/2; this is a strong conventional binary task comparator but not the same as multi-hypothesis estimation or an actual hardware implementation
numerics: Clamp only tiny negative response values in [-2e-8,0], require normalized columns within 2e-8; check the Helstrom one-shot optimum is no worse than fixed readout within 2e-8; preserve exact names, tested source ref and failures.
tests: Mathematically closed synthetic boundary controls including equal, disjoint and overlapping distributions; both real fixtures and all pair inventories must run; no seed selection or outcome-adjusted stopping.
claims: Mathematical finite-case lower-bound audit only. No actual physical shots, real buying intent, monetary cost, measured inference billing, inventor improvement or asset payback.
deployment: NO DEPLOY; all original owner files, legacy ledgers, liability and history unchanged
